notes: Distinct from Computer Science/Software Engineering (profession_11, which covered turning code into products via Indie Hackers) — this category is specifically about the freelance/agency service-delivery side of the same skill. 2026-07-20: Merged in the founder-provided 'web_app_development_resources.csv' (Section I.12), bringing the file from 1 channel / 0 blogs / 0 books to a full 10 / 10 / 10. This CSV (unlike prior ones in this project) did not include per-item RSS/channel-ID URLs, only top-level domains — every real YouTube channel ID was independently looked up via search and channel-page fetches, and blog RSS paths were inferred using each site's standard CMS convention (flagged individually where uncertain). Three of the CSV's 10 channels could not be matched to a real YouTube channel: SoniBaze (real, active company and blog, but no confirmed YouTube presence), FreelanceMaster.ng (real, active company and blog, but no confirmed YouTube presence), and DevCareer Africa (real, well-documented nonprofit with 30,000+ community members, but its 'channels' are internal Slack community channels, not YouTube). Two independently-verified, directly on-topic replacements were substituted to reach 10 channels: freeCodeCamp.org and Programming with Mosh (Mosh Hamedani). The SoniBaze blog URL was also corrected from the source directory's sonibaze.com to the company's real, currently-active domain, sonibaze.ng.
